recheck: jq -r '.gaps[]|"\(.id)\t\(.check)"' data/planning-gaps.json | while IFS=$'\t' read -r id c; do sh -c "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "passing $id" || echo "failing $id"; done

licence.question: Most open manuscript scans (Bodleian, e-codices, Trinity) are CC BY-NC. Keep WorldLibs free and non-commercial?
licence.answer: MIT, open source (user, 2026-11-08). The site stays free; scans and texts keep their holders' licences and load as pointers, never committed.

gallica.question: Gallica blocks scripts. Embed BnF scans or link out?
gallica.answer: Link out (real-browser test 2026-11-08): images fail to load inside another site; BnF books stay catalogue cards with a Gallica link.

ai-reconstruction.question: Where no plan survives, build an AI-assisted reconstruction from cited sources?
ai-reconstruction.answer: yes (user, 2026-11-07): AI fills geometry and decoration only; every element tagged excavated, attested, comparandum or invented; room labelled Reconstruction

globe.question: Entry screen: globe or flat atlas?
globe.answer: Both (2026-11-08): custom three.js globe with NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble KTX2 under 4 MB, terminator on the time slider; it unrolls into the Equal Earth atlas for picking. 'See it today' is a click-to-load MapLibre street: OpenFreeMap tiles, OpenStreetMap 3D buildings, Mapterhorn terrain, free with no key. Google 3D Tiles dropped for cost (owner, 2026-11-08).

renderer.question: WebGL or WebGPU?
renderer.answer: WebGLRenderer by default (2026-11-08). WebGPURenderer only after an A/B test; Spark splats are WebGL2-first.

dynamic-worlds.question: Generate rooms on the device or ship baked rooms?
dynamic-worlds.answer: Split (2026-11-08): a Worker builds geometry from a seeded hall kit on arrival; lightmaps, atlases, props and splats are baked at build time. AI runs at build time only.

gaps.what: Static host fits: Cloudflare Pages free, 20,000 files and 25 MiB per asset, unlimited bandwidth
gaps.note: Texts ship as one JSON per book part (200 KB max), so 127 readable books stay far under 20,000 files.

gaps.what: Every library has a Wikidata QID for live labels and images
Long Room length, width and height proven from a primary source
Long Room bays per side and gallery floor height
gaps.check: jq -e '[.facts[]|select(.lib=="longroom" and .status=="passing" and (.value|test("^(bays per side|gallery floor height)")))]|length==2' data/facts.json
gaps.note: No public source states them. Build with photo estimates scaled from the proven 63.7 m length, tag basis 'estimated', show the tag in the room panel. Optional: ask Trinity Library for drawings.

gaps.what: Long Room reference photos with reuse licence
gaps.note: Per-file CC licences; credits panel must list each file used.

gaps.what: At least five readable public-domain books tied to Trinity (alumni authors)
gaps.note: Swift, Goldsmith, Stoker, Wilde, Synge via Standard Ebooks. Synge's Trinity link is weak (listed, study not proven).

gaps.what: Book of Kells shown without an unlicensed scan
gaps.note: Trinity: Kells images need permission. Phase A shows it as a catalogue card in a glass case.

gaps.what: Phase A acceptance criteria frozen as JSON with checks
Build spec: data schemas, hall kit, delivery and cache, link check, error reports, reconstruction policy, globe, dynamic worlds, living pages, performance
gaps.check: test -s docs/specs/build-spec.md && for h in 'Data files' 'Hall kit' 'Delivery' 'Link check' 'Error reports' 'Reconstruction' 'Globe' 'Dynamic worlds' 'Living pages' 'Performance'; do rg -q "^## $h" docs/specs/build-spec.md || exit 1; done

gaps.what: Manuscript page texture fits a page-turn budget (under 250 KB per page)
gaps.note: Measured Bodleian Folio: 1024w 541 KB, 768w 332 KB, 600w 196 KB, webp 768w 1.0 MB. Rule: 600w for the turning page, region tiles on zoom, prefetch two spreads ahead.

gaps.what: No book sits on a shelf of a library that never held it
gaps.note: 103 general texts and books from holders we do not model (BL, Beinecke) go to a global reading list, not a replica shelf.

gaps.what: Licence: code MIT and open source; scans and texts keep their holders' licences
gaps.note: MIT covers our code and data. Scans load from the holder and are never committed, so CC BY-NC scans stay usable on the free site; a paid fork must drop them.

gaps.what: Similar projects researched, closest competitors named
gaps.note: 17 projects, 16 checked. Closest: The Uncensored Library, the Discovery Tour, MyShelves, Pergamon VR+AI. None combines real rooms, readable books and evidence tags.

gaps.what: Ancient reconstruction briefs: cited elements for Alexandria, Pergamon, Nineveh, Herculaneum, Nalanda, Buda
gaps.note: Cited element lists in data/verify/recon-ancient.json. AI proposes parameters from quotes; people sign off.

gaps.what: Every library has a passing plan, photo set or reconstruction brief
gaps.check: jq -e --slurpfile L data/libs.json --slurpfile R data/verify/recon-ancient.json '($L[0]|map(.id)) - ([.plans[]|select(.status=="passing")|.lib] + [$R[0].facts[]?|select(.field=="recon" and .status=="passing")|.lib]|unique)|length==0' data/facts.json
gaps.note: Measured plans exist only for LoC (1897 Handbook) and Celsus (OAI plan). Every other hall is rebuilt with the hall kit from proven dims plus licensed photos.

gaps.what: No starred (unproven) values left in libs.json
gaps.note: Mafra and Escorial dates proven in the labels pass.

gaps.what: Every library has at least one book row
BnF books: catalogue cards that link out to Gallica (embedding is blocked)
gaps.note: Real-browser test 2026-11-08: Gallica pages and the IIIF manifest open in headed Chrome, but its images fail to load inside another site, plain or CORS (Cloudflare challenge, no cookie). A proxy would be blocked too. So BnF books link out.
